newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FORECAST-SM Prime net seen up in '96, '97.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-SM Prime net seen up in '96, '97.

text.p: SM Prime Holdings Inc, the biggest shopping mall operator in the Philippines, was expected to post a steady net profit growth of about 26 percent in 1996 and 1997 on the back of increased consumer spending, analysts said.
A Reuters poll of six securities firms completed this week showed that SM Prime's net income in 1996 was estimated at an average 1.914 billion pesos, up 26.8 percent from 1.510 billion pesos in 1995.
In the first nine months of 1996, SM Prime's net income rose by 30.7 percent to 1.334 billion pesos from 1.021 billion pesos.
The poll also showed an average projection of 2.404 billion pesos in net income for 1997, up 25.6 percent from the 1996 estimate.
Analysts said SM Prime represents the best play in the retail trade sector in the country.

"Retail trade is expected to improve by at least 15 percent per year, with an anticipated growth in consumption expenditure which accounts for 77 percent of Gross National Product," a report of All Asia Securities said.
Analysts said SM Prime was poised to take maximimum advantage of the increase in consumer expenditure.
